Write the probe: blank space, alignment, boxes, nav stability, the three invariants, the fold, scrollbars
Measure all three at 400/1000/1280/1440/1920/3440 and LOOK at the shots
Judge each page in ten seconds the way the owner would
Fix every finding inside the fence, cause not symptom

assign.now: measured all four pages at six widths and LOOKED at every shot - 11 findings, fixing now

log.msg: THE INSTRUMENT FOUND ITS OWN DEFECTS FIRST, three of them, and each one made a check pass that should have failed. (1) querySelector(".page") returns the FIRST .page in document order, which on this SPA is a hidden one - every measurement came back 0 and the fold check said "above the fold" about a 0x0 box. It is .page.active-page. (2) A custom property does NOT compute to px: getPropertyValue("--gap") hands back the literal clamp() and parseFloat reads NaN, so every blank-space test silently passed. Paint the token on a probe div and measure the div. (3) --measure is 40em, so parseFloat("40em") = 40 and every paragraph on the site was "past the measure". The real ceiling is the element's OWN computed max-width in px. Nothing was judged until all three were fixed.

WHAT PASSES, on all three layouts at 400 / 1000 / 1280 / 1440 / 1920 / 3440. Nothing framed or written at x:0 (only the Catalog's bled BANDS touch the edge, and a band is paint). No prose past its own measure - zero paragraphs over their computed max-width at any width. Zero overflow:auto|scroll boxes and zero clipped scrollers inside any of the three layouts; the page is the only scroller. The first nav element and the layout's own h1 are both above the fold at every width on all three. The hero's height is a vh clamp, 28.9-35.3% of the fold. And the nav is byte-identical before and after opening the fold, and before and after picking tile 18 of 24 on the Workbench: rail box [77,48,240,...] -> [77,48,240,...], 0px change, at all six widths.

RE-DERIVED THE BUILDER'S TABLE, Workbench at 1280, independently. The builder says 8/8. I get 8/8 on the same eight: (a) nothing at x:0; (b) 0 paragraphs over their cap; (c) no constant - every gap/pad/flow in practice.css is a token or a control's own em; (d) the only painted boxes are the tiles and the panel and both are padded, and nothing unpainted carries block padding; (e) one left axis per stacked region; (f) 1177.6/1280 = 0.920; (g) the brand is at y=45.1, the h1 at y=45.1; (h) zero overflow boxes. THE TWO NUMBERS AGREE. The table is not wrong - it is just eight checks the pages can pass while still looking unfinished, which is what the rest of these findings are about.

FINDING 1 - THE WALL HOLES THE FOUR-WIDTH SWEEP COULD NOT SEE. I swept every 80px from 400 to 3440 and counted the columns off the live wall. The Workbench wall (24 tiles) lands on 5 columns from 2240 to 2480 (last row 4 of 5) and on 7 columns from 2880 to 3120 (last row 3 of 7). The Catalog wall (12 cards) lands on 5 columns from 2800 to 3360 - a 560px-wide band of viewport widths that includes a 2880 laptop and any un-maximised window on a 3440 monitor - with a last row of 2 of 5. The builder's "no hole at any width" was proved at four widths and is false between them. CAUSE: repeat(auto-fill, ...) cannot be told which counts are allowed, and 24 and 12 both have gaps in their divisors.

FINDING 2 - THE WORKBENCH WALL STEPS BACKWARDS TWICE as the screen gets WIDER. 2 columns at 720 becomes 1 at 800 (the rail turns into a 240px column at 44rem and takes more than the wall can spare), and 3 columns at 1360 becomes 2 at 1440 (the panel column arrives at 80rem and takes 320 more). At 1440 - a very common laptop - the page shows a 2-column wall that a 1280 laptop shows with 3, and is 2,018px tall for it.

FINDING 3 - THE CATALOG'S CARDS ARE ONE COLUMN FROM 400 ALL THE WAY TO 1040. At 1000 each of the twelve cards is 920px wide while its own sentence stops at its measure, 584px: 336px of empty PAINTED card, twelve times down the page. That is the owner's sentence about padding exactly - a fill with nothing in two thirds of it is not a box, it is a stain.

FINDING 4 - THE CATALOG'S NAV BAR IS TWO THIRDS EMPTY. The eight links huddle in the left third of a painted bar: 2,176px of the 3,260px band is empty at 3440, 878px at 1920, 501px at 1440. Nothing else on the page ends where the links end, so the bar's right-hand two thirds is the single largest blank rectangle on any of the three pages.

FINDING 5 - THE WORKBENCH'S PANEL LEAVES A COLUMN OF NOTHING UP TO 1,940px TALL. At 1440 the panel is 330px tall beside a 2,270px wall; at 1920, 389px beside 1,100. The panel declares position: sticky, but the grid declares align-items: start, so the panel's grid item is exactly as tall as its content and sticky has zero travel - it can never fire. The Reader's own margin comment says the fix (align-self: stretch on the track, sticky on the box inside it); the Workbench did not get it.

FINDING 6 - THE FOLD DOES NOT LINE UP WITH THE PAGE IT IS ABOUT. On the Workbench and the Reader the fold sits OUTSIDE the grid, so its left edge is the page gutter (x=90 at 3440) while the layout's own h1, its rail label column and its wall all start at x=385. A 295px misalignment down the left edge of the page, at every width above 44rem, on the last thing a reader sees.

FINDING 7 - THE READER'S FOUR-COLUMN MARGIN IS THREE TALL GREY RECTANGLES. At 3440 the margin takes the whole leftover (2,213px) and lays four blocks across it in ONE grid row, so the row is as tall as the tallest block: measured tails of 905px and 1,483px under two of the four, and the margin region as a whole ends 726px above the article's bottom. Contents is 5 links in a 520px column; Where next is 3 chips in another. The leftover was spent on WIDTH, and a margin has no more content when it is wider - it just has more empty.

FINDING 8 - THE CATALOG'S CONTENT BAND BUTTS THE FOOTER. The band paints nothing, so by the module's own rule it carries no block padding and takes its air from the painted bands either side - but the footer's air is INSIDE the footer's paint, so there is 0px of the band's own space below its last child: the fold's box ends 12px above the footer's painted top edge at 3440.

FINDING 9 - THE WORKBENCH AT 400 IS A 3,754px STACK, and the panel - the one thing the page exists to demonstrate - is 3,400px down it. Twenty-four full tiles, each with a three-line sentence, in one column. It is not a designed small form; it is the wide form with the columns taken out.

FINDING 10 - THE PRACTICE INDEX AT 1000 SHOWS ONE CARD AND NO SIGN OF THE OTHER TWO. The wall is one column from 400 to 1040, so at 1000 a card is 920px wide with a 920x575 picture in it; the first card's bottom edge is at y=920 against an 800px fold. A reader arriving at 1000 sees one picture and cannot tell there are three.

FINDING 11 - THE CATALOG HERO'S 1,180px MIDDLE, judged and KEPT. At 3440 the hero's words end at x=810 and its two buttons begin at x=1,990. I am calling it wanted, with the reason: the hero BAND is painted (--fill-a04), so that span is a wash and not bare page, and after fixing finding 4 the bar's links, the hero's buttons and the wall's last card all end on one axis at x=3,350 while the brand, the heading and the first card all start on x=90. Both edges of three bands on two axes is a rhythm; it is the only large gap on these pages I did not close.

log.msg: FIXED 1 AND 2 - THE WALL COUNTS ARE WRITTEN OUT NOW, one container query each, and two thresholds moved with them. Re-swept every 80px from 400 to 3440, 39 widths per wall: tiles 2/3/4/6/8 (every one divides 24), cards 1/2/3/4/6 (every one divides 12), index 1/3, Reader margin 1. ZERO holes and the count never decreases as the screen widens. The two thresholds: the rail becomes a column at 48rem instead of 44rem (at 44 what was left could only hold one tile column, which is why 720 -> 800 went backwards), and the panel's floor is 17rem instead of 20rem (which is what lets the wall keep 3 columns across the 80rem switch, fixing 1360 -> 1440). Workbench pageH at 1440: 2,018 -> 1,701px.

FIXED 3 - the card wall is 2 columns at 1000 (cards 452px, text fills), not 1 column of 920px paint holding 584px of sentence. Catalog pageH at 1000: 3,089 -> 2,283px. The four thresholds are written against the BAND'S CONTENT BOX, not the viewport - a band carries padding-inline: var(--gutter-x), so `practice` measures about 92% of the screen and a 58rem threshold missed 1000 (920px = 57.5rem) by half a rem. 57rem catches it.

FIXED 4 - the Catalog's bar spans its band. justify-content: space-between, so the brand stands on x=90 and the last link ends on x=3350 at 3440 - the same two axes the hero's heading and button and the wall's first and last card already stand on. Measured after: brand left 90, h1 left 90, band title left 90, first card left 90, first footer link left 90; nav last right 3350, hero acts right... (see finding 11) and last card right 3350. The 2,176px hole is gone.

FIXED 5 AND the panel's width - the panel sits inside `.std-practice-side`, a stretched unpainted track, and sticks inside it. Measured travel (side height minus panel height): 633px at 3440, 1,029px at 1920, 1,148px at 1440, and 0 at 1280 and below where the panel is under the wall and should not stick. And under the wall it is capped at the measure: 919px of painted box holding 600px of text at 1280 became 602px.

FIXED 6 - the fold is a row of the layout's own grid (`grid-area: why`, areas `rail why why`). At 3440 the Workbench's fold now starts at x=384, the same axis as its h1 (384) and its wall (384); it was at 90. The Reader's fold starts at 1,176, the same axis as its article, and centres with it.

FIXED 7 - THE READER'S MARGIN IS ONE COLUMN AND THE LAYOUT CENTRES, and this is the judgement call of the pass. The margin's four blocks stacked in a 38rem column are 3,496px tall against the article's 2,537, so the region earns its room in HEIGHT rather than in width, and its measured dead tail is 0px at every one of the six widths (was 905 and 1,483). The leftover goes to two equal page gutters - 792px each side at 3440 - which a reader reads as a margin. THE TRADE, said plainly: the Reader's CONTENT now spans 1,568 of 3,440 (0.46) where it used to span 0.948. Check (f) is about the widest painted span and the layout root still spans 0.948, but the honest number is 0.46 and I am not hiding it. The reason: a wall spends a wide screen because it has more items to show, and an article cannot - past 40em a line is tiring - so above its ceiling it holds its measure and centres. The Workbench (8 columns) and the Catalog (6) still fill 3440. Two of three span; the reading page centres.

FIXED 8 - the Catalog's content band has its own air above the footer: `margin-block-end: var(--flow)`. Measured fold-box-bottom to footer-painted-top: 12px -> 45px at 3440, and 28 / 29 / 30 / 32 / 40 at the other five widths. A margin is air between two boxes and not padding inside one, so the module's box rule is untouched.

FIXED 9 - the Workbench's small form is a picker. Below 34rem a tile is its icon and its name in a ROW and the wall is two columns; the sentence it drops is the first line of the panel you get by tapping it, so nothing is deleted. Measured at 400: pageH 3,754 -> 1,750px (-53%), and the panel moved from y=3,400 to y=1,335.

FIXED 10 - the index's card picture is capped at 20rem while the wall is one column. At 1000 the first card's bottom edge moved from y=920 (below an 800px fold) to y=672, so all three names are on the first screen; pageH 2,673 -> 1,632px. At three columns the picture is the whole point and is untouched.

FINDING 11 JUDGED AND KEPT, with the number reduced first. The Catalog hero's words and buttons were 2,007px apart at 3440 because `space-between` ran across the whole 3,260px band. The hero's CONTENT is now capped at 96rem, so the gap is 283px at 3440 and 431px at 1920, and the buttons end on the same axis the fold below them ends on. What is left between them is painted band, not bare page - and a band's middle is paint. That is the one large gap on these three pages that was not closed.

RE-MEASURED EVERYTHING, six widths, three layouts plus the index, after every fix. Still zero: nothing framed or written at x:0, no paragraph past its own computed max-width, no empty rectangle taller than --flow x 3 between two content boxes in any region, no region whose stacked children sit on more than one left axis, no painted box without padding, no unpainted box with block padding, no overflow:auto|scroll box, no clipped scroller, no console error and no failed request on any of the seven urls. The first nav element and the layout's own h1 are above the fold at all six widths on all three. The nav is byte-identical before and after opening the fold and before and after picking tile 18 of 24 - 0px at every width, the same as before the pass. The one measured gap that remains is the Reader's two 792px page gutters, which are the point.

assign.outcome:
**Found 11, fixed 10, kept 1 on purpose — and the three layouts are on the layout wall.**

The three practice layouts landed this afternoon with eight polish checks passing at 400, 1280, 1920 and 3440 — 32 of 32 on every page. This pass measured them at **six** widths, swept the walls **every 80px from 400 to 3440**, and looked at every screenshot. The eight checks are not wrong: re-derived independently on the Workbench at 1280, the two numbers agree. They are eight checks a page can pass while still looking unfinished.

![The Reader at 3440, after](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/practice-critic/shots/after-reader-3440.jpg)

**The biggest one.** Both walls asked `auto-fill` for a column WIDTH, and it cannot be told which counts are allowed. The 24 tiles landed on 5 columns from 2240 to 2480 and on 7 from 2880 to 3120; the 12 cards on 5 from 2800 to 3360 — each a short last row, none of it visible at the four widths it was proved at. The tile wall also stepped BACKWARDS twice as the screen widened. **Both walls write their counts out now**, and a 39-width re-sweep finds no hole anywhere and no count that ever decreases.

**And the one that changes what these three teach.** The Reader's margin used to take the whole leftover at 3440 and lay four blocks across it — 905px and 1,483px of dead ground under two of them. It is one column now and the layout centres above its ceiling: two equal 792px page gutters, and the margin is as tall as the article beside it. A wall can spend a wide screen because it has more items to show; an article cannot, so it holds its measure and centres. The Workbench and the Catalog still fill 3440.

- [**Workbench**](/layouts/practice/workbench/) — 3 columns at 1440 again (was 2), the panel sticks beside the wall instead of leaving up to 1,940px of empty column, and at 400 it is a two-column picker: 3,754px of page became 1,750.
- [**Reader**](/layouts/practice/reader/) — one margin column, zero dead tail at all six widths, the whole layout centred.
- [**Catalog**](/layouts/practice/catalog/) — the nav bar spans its band (2,176px of empty bar gone), the hero's words and buttons are 283px apart instead of 2,007, cards are 2 columns at 1000 instead of one 920px box holding a 584px sentence, and the content band no longer butts the footer.

[**The critic's pass**](/layouts/practice/doc/critique/) is the full record, one click from the module's Docs tab. [`readme.md`](/layouts/practice/) and [`doc/decisions`](/layouts/practice/doc/decisions/) say what changed and why.

**In the browser.** [`/layouts/browse/`](/layouts/browse/) — **102 items in the file, 102 cards on the wall, the Global chip reads 48.** All nine jpegs re-shot after the fixes; each item shows its three widths with the real pixel sizes recorded.

**Left, with the reason.** The Catalog hero keeps 283px between its words and its buttons — that span is painted band, not bare page, and both ends stand on axes the rest of the page uses. And the Reader's CONTENT now spans 0.46 of 3440 rather than 0.948: the layout root still spans 0.948, but the honest number is 0.46, and it is the price of a reading page that centres instead of growing grey.

log.msg:
SKILL IMPROVEMENTS, logged here rather than appended to the skills themselves: `.claude/skills/` is outside this task's write fence (practice/** + this dir + two files in browse/), and the minion skill's own never-list puts the fence above everything. Five lines for whoever can file them.

1. **layout** - `A COLUMN WIDTH CANNOT CONTROL A COLUMN COUNT.` The skill says tiles take `.grid.auto` with a real `--column` in rem so 3440 gets 4+ columns, and that is right about the WIDTH and silent about the COUNT. `auto-fill` lands on whatever fits, so if the item count has gaps in its divisors the wall shows a short last row at widths between the ones you measured: 24 tiles landed on 5 columns over 2240-2480 and on 7 over 2880-3120, 12 cards on 5 over 2800-3360 (2026-09-17). When the item count is fixed, write the counts out as container queries and check every one is a divisor.

2. **layout** - the four widths (400/1280/1920/3440) cannot see a wall hole or a wall that steps BACKWARDS. Both walls above passed at all four. Two things a four-width sweep misses by construction: a count that only appears between two of them, and a count that DROPS when a region arrives (a 2-column wall at 720 became 1 at 800 when the rail turned into a column; 3 at 1360 became 2 at 1440 when the panel arrived). Sweep the count continuously - every 80px from 400 to 3440 is 39 loads and about four minutes.

3. **layout** and **css** - `position: sticky` ON A GRID ITEM UNDER `align-items: start` CAN NEVER FIRE, and nothing throws. The item is exactly as tall as its content, so sticky has zero travel: a panel sat at the top of a column with up to 1,940px of nothing under it and every numeric check passed. The box that stretches and the box that sticks have to be two boxes.

4. **ui-test** - three ways a headless probe on this site silently measures nothing, all three hit in one session. `document.querySelector(".page")` returns the FIRST .page in document order, which is a hidden one - it is `.page.active-page`. `getPropertyValue("--gap")` returns the literal clamp(), never px, so parseFloat reads NaN and every threshold test passes; paint the token on a probe div and measure the div. And `--measure` is `40em`, so parseFloat reads 40 and every paragraph on the site is 'past the measure' - the real ceiling is the element's own computed max-width in px.

5. **documentation** - in the `note(name, title, description)` doc-page shape this site uses, the URL comes from the TITLE and the .md from the first argument. A note named `critique` titled "The critic's pass" routes to /doc/the-critics-pass/, so /doc/critique/ falls through to `Page.file()` and logs a 404 for a page.js that was never going to exist - the exact thing the declared-child note exists to avoid. The title has to slugify to the file name.

CORRECTIONS TO TWO NUMBERS LOGGED ABOVE, and the bug that produced one of them. (1) MY OWN FIX HAD A SPECIFICITY BUG: the compact-tile block was written ABOVE the tile's base rule, and both selectors are (0,2,0) - a container query adds NO specificity - so the later base rule won and the compact tile stayed a column. Nothing warned; it was caught by reading the file back, not by any check. Moved below the base rule, the tile is 44px tall instead of 114px and the Workbench at 400 is 1,405px, not the 1,750 logged above: 3,754 -> 1,405, a 63% cut, with the panel at y=990 instead of y=3,400. (2) The practice index at 1000 is 1,945px, not the 1,632 logged above; the first card's bottom edge is y=677 against an 800px fold (it was y=920), and the second card starts at y=692, so a reader at 1000 now sees that there is more than one. `practice-workbench-400.jpg` was re-shot after the fix and re-copied into browse/shots; its real size still matches the 400 entry in items.json, [400, 1400].
